sections.html:
Lauderdale County's seat is Florence, a river town tucked into Alabama's northwest corner. Huntsville is about 70 miles east on US-72, and Birmingham is about 115 miles to the southeast. The 2020 census counted 40,184 people in 17,516 households, with a median age of 36.4.

Of the 19,710 housing units, 11.1 percent were vacant. Homeowner vacancy ran 2.4% and rental vacancy 8.7%. Median household income was $50,396, so some owners have equity and options while others cannot cover big repairs before a sale.

Streets near the river follow a downtown grid, the blocks around the University of North Alabama are older, and newer subdivisions spread out along US-43 and US-72. Buyers differ from one area to the next, so where your house stands will shape how you market it.

sections.h2: Older houses and what inspectors flag
sections.html:
Florence was laid out in 1818 and incorporated in 1826, so some neighborhoods hold houses well over a century old. Expect original wiring, pipes and foundations in the oldest blocks. Those are the items an FHA or VA inspector, or a bank appraiser, tends to circle.

Write down what has been replaced and what has not. A buyer who sees the whole picture on day one can name a fair price, while surprises found during an inspection tend to kill deals.

Summers are hot and humid and winters run mild to cool. The city collects about 57 inches of rain a year plus a little over two inches of snow, and every drop lands on crawl spaces, roof valleys, gutters and window frames. The city is almost 300 miles from the Gulf, yet Hurricane Katrina's path passed close in 2005 with winds near 70 miles per hour.

Tired roofing is one of the usual reasons a listing sits.

  • Walk the roof line, gutters and flashing before you list. Inspectors start there.
  • Check the crawl space and the lot grading for pooling water.
  • Ask your insurer about wind and hail cover if you are keeping the house a while.

Moving title costs a little: the state levies 50 cents on each $500 of value, a rule found in Alabama Code 40-22-1, and the recording office tacks on a fee of its own. Your deed goes to the Lauderdale County judge of probate along with a form giving the actual price paid.

Refusing to supply that proof once asked brings a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater. A deed that carries only nominal consideration, for example one that corrects a title, is exempt. Clerks there will not write the deed for you, so hire a lawyer or have the title company draw it up.

Values are set at the county courthouse. A lien attaches October 1, payment falls due on the next October 1, and anything unpaid becomes delinquent after December 31. Sell in spring or summer and you will usually owe part of that year's bill at the closing table.

Request a proration from the closing office, and ask them to verify the year is paid before the deed is signed. A tax debt stays with the land, not with the previous owner. Owner-occupied property sits in Alabama's lowest class, assessed at 10 percent of value, and the county tax office can give the exact figure for your parcel.

Three routes are open to you, and they trade time, cost and certainty in different ways.

OptionTime and effortBest fit
List with an agentShowings, repairs, commission and a loan contingency that can fall throughHouse in good shape, no rush
Private saleYou handle marketing, paperwork and negotiationOwner with time and experience
Cash saleCloses on your timeline, house bought as it standsInherited property, tired rentals, houses needing work

Cash Home Buyers quotes Florence houses in their present condition. The number is yours to accept or turn down.

sections.h2: When the house needs major work
sections.html:
Houses that need big repairs are common in older parts of town, and they are the hardest to sell at retail. Lenders want a house that appraises and passes inspection, and many buyers cannot absorb a repair bill on top of a down payment.

When an owner has died and the house sits empty, a probate attorney can say who has authority to sign. Closing waits until the right person can convey title.

  • Pull together the deed, any lender payoff letter and the most recent tax bill.
  • Note what is broken and what still works, so the offer matches reality.
  • Find out how liens or back taxes would be cleared from the proceeds.

sections.h2: What to bring to the closing office
sections.html:
Bring a government photo ID, the deed or trust papers, a lender payoff letter if a mortgage is open, and every key and garage remote. If the house has more than one owner, each of them signs. The title company will tell you if it needs anything else.

If you have already moved, ask the closing office whether you can sign by mail or at a title office near your new home. Plenty of Florence owners live out of town, and the paperwork can usually be handled without a trip back.

sections.h2: If taxes or a mortgage are still owed
sections.html:
Owing money does not block a sale. A lender's payoff letter gives the exact amount to clear, and the closing office pays it from your proceeds before sending you the rest. Back taxes work the same way, because they attach to the land and must be paid off for the buyer to receive clear title.

Ask for the payoff figure and the tax balance before you accept anything. Knowing both lets you see what you would take home and decide with real numbers.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or rental house
sections.html:
Inherited houses and tired rentals make up much of the cash market in Florence. With a rental, tell the buyer whether tenants are staying, and have the lease and deposit records ready. With an inherited house, settle who is allowed to sign first, because a buyer can only close with the person who holds legal authority.

In both cases, the earlier you collect the deed, the tax bill and any payoff letter, the sooner a firm offer can be made.

sections.h2: Timeline for a Florence cash sale
sections.html:
With a clean title, closing is a matter of weeks. An estate or an unpaid lien adds time, since each needs its own paperwork before a deed can pass. The order runs like this: you ask for an offer, the buyer looks the house over, a contract is signed, the record is searched, and the deed is filed in Lauderdale County.

Houses near campus attract investors and families tied to the university, and farther-out subdivisions draw people who want to live in the house. Tell the buyer which side of town you are on and whether the house has been a rental or a family home.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house in Florence, AL as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers accept the present condition and build repair costs into the price. Ask a lawyer or title agent what you must disclose.

faqs.q: How is the deed tax figured when selling in Florence?
faqs.a: The state charges 50 cents per $500 of value, and the recording office adds a fee. Staff work out the total when the deed is filed.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Lauderdale County?
faqs.a: Payment is due October 1 and late after December 31. A mid-year sale normally splits the bill between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: Do I need an attorney to sell my Florence house?
faqs.a: Usually a title company or lawyer runs the closing. Probate clerks will not prepare a deed, so a professional drafts it.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale close in Florence?
faqs.a: Weeks, when the title is clean. Probate and liens stretch that out.
